title: Microsoft Edge: Enhanced Security Mode Plus adds admin-set restrictions on top of Enhanced Security Mode
summary: The briefing accurately separates the planned Plus controls from the existing Edge policies. The roadmap facts and both existing policies' Group Policy paths and registry settings are supported; independent searches found no published Plus control, default or licensing requirement.

claims.claim: Existing ESM disables just-in-time JavaScript compilation.
claims.quote: Enhanced security mode in Microsoft Edge mitigates memory-related vulnerabilities by disabling just-in-time (JIT) JavaScript compilation

claims.claim: Existing ESM enables additional operating system protections.
claims.quote: enabling additional operating system protections for the browser.

claims.claim: Learn documents an ESM user setting called Enhance your security on the web.
claims.quote: Under Security, verify that Enhance your security on the web is enabled.

claims.claim: Learn describes Off as the existing ESM user setting's default choice.
claims.quote: Toggle Off (Default): Feature is turned off

claims.claim: The existing ESM user setting offers Balanced.
claims.quote: Toggle On – Balanced (Recommended)

claims.claim: The existing ESM user setting offers Strict.
claims.quote: Toggle On – Strict

claims.claim: Some users might see existing ESM enabled by default because of ongoing development and testing.
claims.quote: Some users might see enhanced security turned on by default due to ongoing development and testing.

claims.claim: Learn warns that users of Strict ESM may have challenges accomplishing their usual tasks.
claims.quote: Toggle On – Strict: Microsoft Edge will apply added security protections for all the sites a user visits. Users may report some challenges accomplishing their usual tasks.

claims.claim: The roadmap description concerns browser restrictions and names no new data Edge reads or sends.
claims.quote: Admins can configure preset or custom modes to restrict selected network protocols and compression behavior, hardware-access web APIs, WebGL, and external protocol launches when Enhanced Security Mode is enabled.

claims.claim: The roadmap description involves no agent or automated action.
claims.quote: Admins can configure preset or custom modes to restrict selected network protocols and compression behavior, hardware-access web APIs, WebGL, and external protocol launches when Enhanced Security Mode is enabled.

claims.claim: The ESM Group Policy path is Administrative Templates > Microsoft Edge > Enhance the security state in Microsoft Edge.
claims.quote: Group Policy (ADMX) info; GP name: Enhance the security state in Microsoft Edge; GP path (Mandatory): Administrative Templates/Microsoft Edge

claims.claim: The ESM registry setting is SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Edge, value EnhanceSecurityMode, type REG_DWORD.
claims.quote: Registry settings; Path (Mandatory): SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Edge; Value name: EnhanceSecurityMode; Value type: REG\_DWORD

claims.claim: EnhanceSecurityMode value 0 is StandardMode, which turns ESM off and therefore does not satisfy Plus's stated ESM-enabled condition.
claims.quote: If you set this policy to 'StandardMode', the enhanced mode is turned off, and Microsoft Edge falls back to its standard security mode. StandardMode (0) = Standard mode

claims.claim: EnhanceSecurityMode value 1 selects BalancedMode.
claims.quote: BalancedMode (1) = Balanced mode

claims.claim: EnhanceSecurityMode value 2 selects StrictMode.
claims.quote: StrictMode (2) = Strict mode

claims.claim: The existing EnhanceSecurityMode policy is per profile.
claims.quote: Per Profile: Yes

claims.claim: Existing EnhanceSecurityMode is supported on Windows from version 98.
claims.quote: Windows: ≥ 98

claims.claim: Existing EnhanceSecurityMode is supported on macOS from version 98.
claims.quote: macOS: ≥ 98

claims.claim: Existing EnhanceSecurityMode is not supported on Android.
claims.quote: Android: Not supported

claims.claim: Existing EnhanceSecurityMode is not supported on iOS.
claims.quote: iOS: Not supported

claims.quote: Searched: "Enhanced Security Mode Plus" default unconfigured rollout platforms administrator role scope. Read roadmap and opened EnhanceSecurityMode, browse-safer and Edge policy index; existing ESM support is documented, but no Plus version or platform limits were found.

claims.claim: The WebGL policy's Group Policy path is Administrative Templates > Microsoft Edge > Disable support for 3D graphics APIs.
claims.quote: Group Policy (ADMX) info; GP name: Disable support for 3D graphics APIs; GP path (Mandatory): Administrative Templates/Microsoft Edge

claims.claim: The WebGL policy's registry setting is SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Edge, value Disable3DAPIs, type REG_DWORD.
claims.quote: Registry settings; Path (Mandatory): SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Edge; Value name: Disable3DAPIs; Value type: REG\_DWORD

claims.where: controls[2].governs; Governance guidance: At rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: Disable3DAPIs can block web pages from accessing WebGL.
claims.quote: Prevent web pages from accessing the graphics processing unit (GPU). Specifically, web pages can't access the WebGL API

claims.claim: Disable3DAPIs also blocks plug-ins from using the Pepper 3D API.
claims.quote: plug-ins can't use the Pepper 3D API.

claims.claim: Disable3DAPIs covers those graphics APIs, not Plus's network protocols, hardware-access web APIs or external protocol launches.
claims.quote: Prevent web pages from accessing the graphics processing unit (GPU). Specifically, web pages can't access the WebGL API and plug-ins can't use the Pepper 3D API.

claims.claim: Disable3DAPIs is per profile.
claims.quote: Per Profile: Yes

claims.claim: Disable3DAPIs does not apply to a profile signed in with a Microsoft account.
claims.quote: Applies to a profile that is signed in with a Microsoft account: No

claims.where: controls[2].note; Governance guidance: At rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: Disable3DAPIs is an existing separate graphics policy, not a Plus setting.
claims.quote: Windows: ≥ 77; macOS: ≥ 77; Prevent web pages from accessing the graphics processing unit (GPU). Specifically, web pages can't access the WebGL API and plug-ins can't use the Pepper 3D API.

claims.claim: The EnhanceSecurityMode policy page does not mention Plus.
claims.quote: Searched: "Enhanced Security Mode Plus" Edge policy registry preset custom modes. Opened and read the entire EnhanceSecurityMode reference; it describes StandardMode, BalancedMode, StrictMode and deprecated BasicMode, with no mention of Plus.

claims.claim: The cited policy pages do not state a required role for setting the existing policies.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Edge Enhanced Security Mode Plus configure permissions administrator Group Policy. Opened and read EnhanceSecurityMode and Disable3DAPIs in full; both give policy and registry settings but name no required role. Browse-safer refers generically to Enterprise Admins.
